analyzed_vuln.description: In the FLAG_NUM branch, comma-terminated numeric components are parsed with atoi() and checked only for i >= DEFAULTFLAGS, unlike the final component which also rejects i < 0. Thus an intermediate negative flag is cast directly to unsigned short. For -25 this becomes 65511, exactly ONLYUPCASEFLAG. When this malformed vector is stored as an AF alias and a dictionary entry /1 borrows that alias pointer, free_flag() sees ONLYUPCASEFLAG and incorrectly treats the borrowed vector as independently owned: free_table() deletes it, then HashMgr::~HashMgr() deletes the same pointer again from aliasf, causing the reported double-free.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Attacker-controlled affix data must select FLAG num and define an AF alias whose non-final comma-separated component is a suitable negative integer (the PoV uses AF -25,5, where (unsigned short)-25 == ONLYUPCASEFLAG). Dictionary data must contain a word referencing that alias (the PoV uses /1), causing get_aliasf() to place the shared aliasf pointer into an hentry. On HashMgr destruction, free_table() first frees the pointer because the forged flag vector contains ONLYUPCASEFLAG, and the subsequent aliasf cleanup frees it again. The fuzzer input supplies the word-length prefix, then splits the remaining attacker bytes into the .aff and .dic files.
